newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currencies ended mostly lower, but key contracts closed above support levels as dollar buying dried up despite gains in the U.S. asset markets.
Initially, the rally in U.S. bonds and stocks sparked dealer selling in the yen futures, traders said. Sell-stop orders heavy from $0.007922 to $0.7919, they said.
June yen set a contract low at $0.007916 around midday, as the dollar pierced resistance at 126.96 spot yen and rose to the year's high of 127.14 spot.
They said U.S. asset markets were rallying on hopes that a U.S. budget deal would soon be reached.

U.S. House Ways and Means Committee chairman Bill Archer said Wednesday that the White House and congressional Republicans were "pretty close on the tax side" as part of a five-year balanced budget deal.
In addition, U.S. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he thought differences with the White House over tax cut proposals could be resolved.
Republicans have said they want a $100 billion net tax cut over five years, while the administration has asked for a gross tax cut of $98 billion offset by $76 billion in tax hikes.
"If we get a budget agreement, that will be even more positive for the dollar," one currency futures trader said.
Floor traders said a budget deal would stabilize long bond yields, which would be another plus for the dollar.
However, floor traders noted an immediate lack of selling interest when June yen fell to $0.007916.
June yen gravitated back above $0.007919, which currently corresponds to the 127.14 level.
Meanwhile, June marks held above the day's low of $0.5781, which is fractionally higher than support at $0.5780, or about 1.7350 spot.
Some traders and analysts attributed the lack of activity in part to the May Day holiday in most European countries on Thursday.
Traders may have also stayed on the sidelines ahead of another round of U.S. data on Thursday.

U.S. March personal income and consumption figures, along with weekly jobless claims and the April National Association of Purchasing Management index, will be released within the first 90 minutes of pit trade. U.S. March construction spending will also be released on Thursday morning.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000012 at $0.007925, marks were off $0.0021 at $0.5800, Swiss francs were $0.0022 lower at $0.6829, sterling was down $.0082 at $1.6226, Canadian dollars were up $0.0002 at $0.7179, Australian dollars were down $0.0008 at $0.7806, and Mexican pesos were $0.000325 higher at $0.123625.
